summary: thedata exports an opaque encrypted blob as its sole functionality
details: Package thedata@1.0.9 consists of a single export: index.js re-exports `desKey` from apps/docs/app/theta.js, which reads the sibling file apps/docs/app/des.db (a base64-wrapped OpenSSL 'Salted__' ciphertext of ~37KB when decoded) via readFileSync and exports its contents as a string. The package's stated purpose ('Theta Data API docs') is not consistent with shipping and exporting an encrypted binary blob as its entire functionality. The package itself performs no install-time or import-time actions against the installer: there are no lifecycle hooks in package.json, no network I/O, no child_process/exec calls, no reads of installer secrets or environment variables, and no dynamic evaluation of the blob's contents. The encrypted payload is inert within this package — it becomes meaningful only if a separate consumer imports `desKey`, decrypts it with a key held elsewhere, and executes or interprets the plaintext.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
